newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs end up; bad debt clearing plan ignored.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs end up; bad debt clearing plan ignored.

text.p: South Korean stocks closed higher on Wednesday as individual stocks rose on bargain hunting, but the government's plan to set up a 1.5 trillion won fund to liquidate bank bad debts was ignored, brokers said.
Jinro Ltd, which defaulted on debt payments on Monday, resumed trading after a one-day trading halt and closed 720 won lower at its daily limit of 8,350.
The composite index ended up 5.09 points at 693.05.
"It's a token effort, frankly," said Richard Samuelson, head of research at SBC Warburg. "1.5 trillion won is not nearly large enough."
"History is history. The real issue for South Korea is: will the government continue to tinker in bank lending," Samuelson said.
The finance ministry said the fund, to be financed mainly with contributions from banks, bond issues and borrowings, would be operated for five years.

Jinro Ltd's parent, the nation's 19th-ranked Jinro Group, has been in financial trouble under heavy debts valued at 3.2 trillion won. The group said last week it would sell some of its property and affiliates to raise cash to pay back debt.
Chung Won Corp, which resumed trading at its lower limit after a one-day trading halt on Tuesday, closed 500 won higher at its upper limit of 6,830.
Chung Won on Monday failed to honour 800 million worth of promissory notes but said on Tuesday it had settled the payments by the legal deadline set at the close of Tuesday.
Among big gainers are Sewoo Polymer that ended up 1,700 won at its limit of 23,100 and Dong-A Pharmaceutical that gained 1,700 won to its limit of 23,100.
